flawed_step: The claim incorrectly asserts that closed singletons guarantee disjoint open neighbourhoods for distinct points.
counterexample: Let X = N with the cofinite topology: the open sets are ∅ and all subsets U whose complement X\U is finite. Every singleton {n} is closed because X\{n} is open, so X is T1. However, any two nonempty open sets intersect: if U and V were disjoint, then X = (X\U) ∪ (X\V) would be finite, a contradiction. Thus the distinct points 0 and 1 have no disjoint open neighbourhoods, so X is not Hausdorff.
assessment_summary: The cofinite topology on an infinite set is T1 but not Hausdorff, directly refuting the statement.
